I=\int\sqrt{x-x^{2}}\,dx
\]

---

### 1.  Complete the square  

\[
x-x^{2}= -\Bigl(x^{2}-x\Bigr)=\frac14-\Bigl(x-\frac12\Bigr)^{2}.
\]

Hence  

\[
\sqrt{x-x^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac14-\Bigl(x-\frac12\Bigr)^{2}}
          =\frac12\sqrt{1-(2x-1)^{2}} .
\]

---

### 2.  Trigonometric substitution  

Set  

\[
u=2x-1\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x=\frac{u+1}{2},\;dx=\frac{du}{2}.
\]

Then  

\[
I=\int\frac12\sqrt{1-u^{2}}\;\frac{du}{2}
   =\frac14\int\sqrt{1-u^{2}}\,du .
\]

---

### 3.  Integrate \(\sqrt{1-u^{2}}\)

A standard antiderivative is  

\[
\int\sqrt{1-u^{2}}\;du
   =\frac{u}{2}\sqrt{1-u^{2}}+\frac12\arcsin u +C.
\]

Multiplying by \(\tfrac14\),

\[
I=\frac18\,u\sqrt{1-u^{2}}+\frac18\arcsin u +C .
\]

---

### 4.  Return to the variable \(x\)

Recall \(u=2x-1\) and  
\(\sqrt{1-u^{2}}= \sqrt{1-(2x-1)^{2}}
                = 2\sqrt{x-x^{2}}\).

Thus  

\[
\frac18 u\sqrt{1-u^{2}}
   =\frac18(2x-1)\cdot 2\sqrt{x-x^{2}}
   =\frac14\,(2x-1)\sqrt{x-x^{2}} .
\]

Finally  

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle 
\int\sqrt{x-x^{2}}\,dx
   =\frac{(2x-1)\sqrt{x-x^{2}}}{4}
     +\frac{1}{8}\,\arcsin(2x-1)+C }.
\]

---

(Using \(\arcsin(2x-1)=2\arcsin\sqrt{x}-\frac{\pi}{2}\), the antiderivative can also be written as  
\(\displaystyle \frac{(2x-1)\sqrt{x-x^{2}}}{4}+\frac14\arcsin\!\sqrt{x}+C\).)<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
